title: AI Estate
description: What your AI usage is worth at official API list prices, where it went (provider, model, tokens), your real Codex limits and the local GPU box. Pick a period with the time picker or the This month / Last month buttons; totals follow it. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-aiobs-list-value-readable-dashboard-design.md.

panels.description: What this period's AI usage would cost at the vendors' official API list prices -- Claude Code, Codex (including Fast and Ultrafast) and Droid -- plus real OpenRouter spend. Claude and Codex are subscriptions, so this is value used, not money charged. Models with no official price use tokscale's estimate (Pricing column in Models). Follows the time picker.

panels.title: Astra speed mix
panels.description: Astra tokens this period by speed tier. Fast costs 2x and Ultrafast 6x the Standard API price (your plan allowance burns 2.5x / 8x). Speed is recorded from 26 Sep 2026; earlier usage shows as Unknown and is valued at Standard.

panels.title: Codex weekly limit & credits
panels.description: Weekly limit used (left axis) and purchased credits left (right axis), from your Codex logs.

panels.title: Serving
panels.description: Which engine and model the inference server on the GPU box is running right now (vLLM, SGLang or llama.cpp; llama.cpp exposes no model label). Offline = no engine metrics in the last 2 minutes.

panels.title: Inference Engine
panels.description: Live load and cache state of the resident engine: requests running and queued, KV-cache occupancy (vLLM kv_cache_usage_perc / SGLang token_usage), prefix-cache hit rate (cached prompt tokens / prompt tokens) and completed requests -- the last two over the dashboard time range.

panels.title: GPU Power
panels.description: Board power draw on the GPU box against its enforced power limit (dashed). The axis keeps the whole power budget in view, so idle reads as idle.

panels.title: GPU Utilization & VRAM
panels.description: SM utilization and VRAM occupancy, both as a share of capacity on one 0-100% axis (VRAM sits near the engine's reservation, e.g. vLLM gpu_memory_utilization, whenever a model is loaded).

panels.title: GPU Vitals
panels.description: Energy since local midnight plus the latest die temperature, fan duty, graphics clock and VRAM in use on the GPU box -- always the present, whatever the dashboard range (instant queries pinned to now and to local midnight, see zoom_safe). Energy is MetricsQL integrate() over the actual power samples, in kWh -- deliberately NOT avg_over_time(...) * $__range_s, which extrapolates the sampled average across unsampled hours and over-reported ~3.4x on a partial-coverage day (drifting DOWNWARD as idle samples accumulated); caught 2026-08-29 against a raw /api/v1/export trapezoid ground truth (integrate() matched within 0.25%). integrate() wraps the raw selector: integrate(max(m)[..]) is an implicit subquery that resamples and read 0.85% high (2026-09-27). Evaluated as an instant query over (midnight, now]: the RANGE path of integrate() carries the last reading through an outage (read 27% high for 10 Sep), the instant path does not.

panels.title: Generation Throughput
panels.description: Decode tokens per second across whichever engine is resident (one __name__ regex over vLLM, SGLang and both llama.cpp spellings; keep_metric_names prevents duplicate-series collisions). $__rate_interval widens with the step so long ranges average instead of aliasing.

panels.title: Prompt Throughput
panels.description: Prompt tokens per second the engine actually computed (prefill work), across engines -- prefix-cache hits are left out: vLLM and SGLang prompt totals include them (vLLM counted cache hits as prefill about 5.7x over) while llama.cpp's do not, so each engine's computed-only counter is used. Split from generation on purpose: prefill runs 10-30x faster than decode and would flatten it on a shared axis.

panels.title: Latency (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Time to first token and end-to-end request latency from the engine's own histograms (vLLM and SGLang expose both; llama.cpp has no latency histogram). Gaps mean no requests in that window.

panels.title: Estate Timeline
panels.description: History of every moving part over the dashboard range: which inference engine was resident on the GPU box, whether the LLM server and GPU exporter answered their scrapes (worst state per step), and whether each collector lane succeeded (a push every 10 minutes; 20-minute window). Empty = no data at all -- the box or collector was off.

panels.title: Collector Lanes
panels.description: Current state of each data path. Status: a collector lane is up when it succeeded in the last 20 minutes; a scrape is up when the last scrape in 2 minutes answered (a signal seen in the last 30 days but silent now reads down). Last seen: time since the lane's last success (aiobs_lane_last_success_timestamp) or since the last sample actually arrived (tlast_over_time) -- green under 15 minutes, amber under an hour, red beyond. Health gauges are wrapped in last_over_time because a bare instant selector's ~5-minute staleness lookback is shorter than the collector's 600 s push cadence.

targets.expr: (max by (signal)(label_replace(last_over_time(aiobs_lane_up[20m]) or (last_over_time(aiobs_lane_up[30d]) * 0), "signal", "$1 lane", "lane", "(.*)")) or max by (signal)(label_replace(label_replace(last_over_time(up{job=~"gpu|llm"}[2m]) or (last_over_time(up{job=~"gpu|llm"}[30d]) * 0), "signal", "GPU exporter", "job", "gpu"), "signal", "LLM server", "job", "llm"))) @ now()

(max by (signal)(label_replace(now() - last_over_time(aiobs_lane_last_success_timestamp[30d]), "signal", "$1 lane", "lane", "(.*)")) or label_set(now() - max(tlast_over_time(nvidia_smi_power_draw_watts[30d])), "signal", "GPU exporter") or label_set(now() - max(tlast_over_time({__name__=~"vllm:num_requests_running|sglang:num_running_reqs|llamacpp:requests_processing"}[30d])), "signal", "LLM server")) @ now()

panels.title: Hermes Client View
panels.description: Daily tokens by Hermes model/profile as tokscale sees Hermes on the client side -- a mix of local-served and cloud-routed traffic, so it is never summed into any cross-provider total here (anti-double-count rule). One bar per local day, today last (same forward-looking two-point subtraction as the cloud panels, not increase()).

targets.expr: topk_max(12, sum by (model)(max_over_time(aiobs_tokens_total{provider="hermes",origin="client"}[400d] offset -1d) - (max_over_time(aiobs_tokens_total{provider="hermes",origin="client"}[400d]) or (max_over_time(aiobs_tokens_total{provider="hermes",origin="client"}[400d] offset -1d)*0))) > 0)
